hints: Focus on what each molecule can do between its own molecules, since boiling breaks intermolecular forces, not covalent bonds.
Check for an O-H group, as only a molecule with H directly attached to O can donate a hydrogen bond to itself.
Remember that hydrogen bonding is much stronger than permanent dipole-dipole forces, so the hydrogen-bonded liquid will need the most energy to boil.
walkthrough:
**Look at the functional groups**

All three have a similar $M_r$ around 44 to 46, so size is not the deciding factor. What matters is the type of intermolecular force each can form.

$\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$ has $\text{C=O}$, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$ has $\text{O-H}$, $\text{CH}_3\text{OCH}_3$ has $\text{C-O-C}$

**Decide who can hydrogen bond to itself**

Hydrogen bonding between like molecules needs H attached directly to N or O. Only ethanol has this.

$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{O-H} \cdots \text{O(H)C}_2\text{H}_5$ is a hydrogen bond

**Rank the forces and boiling points**

Ethanol has hydrogen bonds plus permanent dipole-dipole and London forces. Ethanal and methoxymethane are polar but have no O-H, so they only have permanent dipole-dipole forces plus London forces as their strongest attraction.

Strength: hydrogen bonds > permanent dipole-dipole forces

**Pick the highest boiling point**

Stronger forces need more thermal energy to separate the molecules. So ethanol has the highest boiling point, caused by hydrogen bonding.

options.A: Incorrect. Methoxymethane, $\text{CH}_3\text{OCH}_3$, is polar so it has permanent dipole-dipole forces, but it has no O-H bond and cannot donate hydrogen bonds to itself. It actually has the lowest boiling point of the three.
options.B: Incorrect. Ethanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$, is polar but it has no H attached to O, only C-H and C=O. It cannot form hydrogen bonds between its own molecules, so this pairing of compound and interaction is wrong.
options.C: Correct. Ethanol, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$, has an O-H group and forms strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds between its molecules. These are stronger than the permanent dipole-dipole forces in the other two, giving ethanol the highest boiling point.
options.D: Incorrect. The interaction is right for ethanal, as $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$ does have permanent dipole-dipole forces as its strongest force, but ethanal does not have the highest boiling point. Ethanol beats it because hydrogen bonding is stronger.
